newsitem.title: THAILAND: Honda opens ASEAN head office in Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: Honda opens ASEAN head office in Bangkok.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had made Thailand its Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) headquarters.

The decision reflected the country's role as a major manufacturing base for Honda's cars and motorcycles in Asia, said Satoshi Toshida, chief executive of Asian Honda Motor Co Ltd, at a ceremony to mark the occasion.
ASEAN groups Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Brunei and Vietnam.

Honda would mark a corporate milestone of selling more than 10 million engine-powered products during the Japanese fiscal year ending March 1997. He said more than 1.4 million of those products would be produced in Thailand.

Honda exports Thai-produced auto components, motorcycles and engine products to more than 40 countries and it accounts for nearly 90 percent of Thai motorcycle exports, worth 5.4 billion baht ($216 million) a year.

Toshida said Honda had located one of its three regional production bases outside Japan in Thailand because of the country's "stable policy environment designed to encourage international competitiveness rather than domestic industry protection, which has resulted in a rapid increase in international investment".
General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co announced earlier this year plans to open their Asian production facilities in Thailand.
Thailand is the world's third biggest motorcycle market after China and India and Honda holds a 52 percent share.
Toshida said Honda operates the world biggest motorcycle plant in Thailand with an annual capacity of more than one million units.
